accordion/border/color.note: accordion.scss:11 — --accordion-border-color: var(--uids-gray-light); uids-core.scss:31 --uids-gray-light: var(--uiowa-color-gray-200) (#CACACA). ONE shared token covers both the default and white colorways.

accordion/content/background.note: accordion.scss:71 — background-color: variables.$white = literal #fff (_variables.scss:29), flat, no brandChannel. accordion/icon/gap.note: accordion.scss:45 — margin: -0.3rem .7rem 0 0; (the margin-right component only). accordion/icon/size.note: accordion.scss:40-41 — width: variables.$h5-font-size; height: variables.$h5-font-size; = 1.4rem (font-size.300, 'h5 clamp large end' per tokens/primitives/typography.json). accordion/outline/color.note: accordion.scss:10 — --accordion-outline-color: var(--uids-gray-cool); uids-core.scss:24 --uids-gray-cool: var(--uiowa-color-gray-500) (#63666A). accordion/white/label/color.note: accordion.scss:104 — --accordion-label-color: #{variables.$white} (literal #fff). Overrides the default colorway's accordion/label/color (gray.100) when .accordion--white is active.

accordion/white/label/color-hover.note: accordion.scss:105 — --accordion-label-color-hover: var(--uids-light) (#F3F3F3 — the SAME primitive as the default colorway's resting label-color, token accordion/label/color above). This IS a real, active override (unlike border-color below): the white colorway's hover state genuinely renders gray/100 where the default colorway's hover renders the new lighter-gray primitive instead. Kept as its own leaf despite the value coincidence, matching the Headline precedent of multiple distinct tokens sharing one primitive value (headline.highlight.color and headline.highlight.background-on-gold both = {color.black}).

alert/border-radius.note: alert.scss:8 border-radius: 2px;. Raw literal — no radius primitive scale exists anywhere in tokens/ yet (only colors.json/typography.json/spacing.json under primitives/), and 2px is a genuine deviation from the platform's otherwise-universal-0 border-radius ($border-radius/-lg/-sm all 0, _variables.scss:39-41). See openQuestions re: whether this warrants a shared radius tier.

alert/danger/background.note: alert.scss:62 background: variables.$danger-light. _variables.scss:20 $danger-light: color.scale($danger, $lightness: 85%). EXISTING primitive — already minted (tokens/primitives/colors.json) during the Forms migration for the error-input background; reused verbatim here, not re-minted.

alert/danger/icon-color.note: alert.scss:65 color: variables.$danger (inside .fa-circle). _variables.scss:19 $danger: #BD472A (literal hex). EXISTING primitive.

alert/dismiss/icon-font-size.note: alert.scss:126-128 i { font-size: 1.5rem; } inside .alert--dismissible button. Raw literal — deliberately NOT aliased to space.150 despite the numeric coincidence (also 1.5rem): that primitive lives in the spacing category and this is a font-size property, so cross-category aliasing would be semantically misleading and could bind the wrong Figma variable scope. See claims for a markup-tag caveat on this rule's selector.

alert/dismiss/size.note: alert.scss:123-124 height: 42px; width: 42px; on .alert--dismissible button (square hit target). Raw literal — no matching dimension primitive. Flag: 2px short of the WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) 44x44px recommended minimum target size; well clear of WCAG 2.2's 2.5.8 (AA) 24x24px minimum. Tokenize as-shipped; see openQuestions.

alert/heading/h2.note: alert.scss:7,15 --h2-font-size: 1.6rem (component-local custom property) / h2 { font-size: var(--h2-font-size); }. Coincidentally matches the EXISTING typography.font-size.400 primitive (1.6rem/25.6px) exactly — reused, though that primitive's own comment documents an UNRELATED origin ('h4 clamp large end; .is-large; intro clamps small end'). This is Alert's own PRIVATE internal heading de-escalation scale, wholly independent of the site's real global h2 ($h2-font-size / --uiowa-font-size-heading-h2, e.g. consumed by card.scss:223) despite sharing the coincidental name 'h2' — verified: --h2-font-size (the custom property) appears only in alert.scss; $h2-font-size (the Sass var) appears only in _variables.scss:65 and card.scss:223.

alert/heading/h3.note: alert.scss:18 font-size: calc(0.9 * var(--h2-font-size)); = 0.9 x 1.6rem = 1.44rem (23.04px). Resolved to a concrete value because Figma text styles cannot bind calc() expressions — see openQuestions for the alternative (base + ratio-set) the input survey raised. Raw literal: no existing font-size primitive equals 1.44rem (nearest neighbors: font-size.325=1.425rem, font-size.350=1.45rem); single alert-internal consumer, not promoted to a new primitive.

alert/heading/h4.note: alert.scss:21 calc(0.8 * var(--h2-font-size)) = 1.28rem (20.48px). Raw literal, same reasoning as h3 (nearest neighbors: font-size.200=1.25rem, font-size.250=1.3rem).

alert/heading/h5.note: alert.scss:24 calc(0.7 * var(--h2-font-size)) = 1.12rem (17.92px). Raw literal, same reasoning (nearest neighbors: font-size.125=1.1rem, font-size.150=1.2rem).

alert/heading/h6.note: alert.scss:27 calc(0.6 * var(--h2-font-size)) = 0.96rem (15.36px). Raw literal, same reasoning (nearest neighbors: font-size.75=0.9rem, font-size.100=1rem).

alert/icon/gap.note: alert.scss:43 .alert__icon { padding: 0 1.5rem 0 0; } — the gap between the icon block and the body content. Same space.150 primitive as alert/padding (coincidentally equal values today); modeled as a separate token because it is a semantically distinct property (icon-to-content gap vs. the component's own edge padding), matching how Button keeps icon-gap and padding-inline as independent tokens despite both being spacing values.

alert/info/background.note: alert.scss:90 background: variables.$info-light. _variables.scss:16 $info-light: color.scale($info, $lightness: 95%). NEW primitive — see newPrimitives.

alert/info/icon-color.note: alert.scss:93 color: variables.$info (inside .fa-circle). _variables.scss:15 $info: #00558C (literal hex; coincidentally the same value as color.blue / $link-color, but a separately-named primitive already exists for that reason — same non-issue as gold/warning). EXISTING primitive.

alert/line-height.note: alert.scss:10 line-height: 1.3; on the base .alert. Coincidentally matches the EXISTING typography.line-height.130 primitive exactly — reused. IMPORTANT: this value visually applies only to .alert itself and its FIRST child; every subsequent sibling gets line-height:1.6 instead via the higher-specificity '* + *:not(...)' rule (specificity (0,1,3) beats .alert's (0,1,0) — verified by direct specificity calculation) — see geometryNotTokenized.sibling-spacing-reset.

alert/padding.note: alert.scss:9 padding: 1.5rem; on the base .alert (uniform on all four sides — no asymmetry to model, unlike Button's block-start/block-end/inline split). Coincidentally matches the EXISTING space.150 primitive (tokens/primitives/spacing.json, currently commented for an unrelated uids_base grid-gap use) exactly — reused per the same reuse-over-reinvent rule already established for $orange/color.status.danger.

alert/success/background.note: alert.scss:70 background: variables.$success-light. _variables.scss:14 $success-light: color.scale($success, $lightness: 95%). NEW primitive — see newPrimitives.

alert/success/icon-color.note: alert.scss:73 color: variables.$success (inside .fa-circle). _variables.scss:13 $success: #00664F (literal hex). EXISTING primitive.

alert/warning/background.note: alert.scss:78 background: variables.$warning-light. _variables.scss:18 $warning-light: color.scale($warning, $lightness: 85%) — 85%, not 95% like success/info; see knownIssues (lightness-scale inconsistency). NEW primitive — see newPrimitives.

alert/warning/icon-color.note: alert.scss:81 color: variables.$orange (inside .fa-circle, nested under .alert--warning). _variables.scss:12 $orange: #BD472A — bit-identical to $danger (_variables.scss:19, also #BD472A). Deliberately reuses the EXISTING color.status.danger primitive (its own comment in tokens/primitives/colors.json already reads '4.x: $danger / $orange') rather than minting a redundant color.status.warning-icon or color.status.orange. Visible consequence: the warning state's icon renders in the same red as the danger state's icon, never in any shade of the actual $warning yellow (#FFCD00). See claims.

badge/blue/background.note: badge.scss:29 — background: variables.$info, a literal #00558C (_variables.scss:15). Flat. CAUTION: #00558C is ALSO the exact value of the separate {color.blue} primitive ('Link blue', tokens/primitives/colors.json) — but the actual Sass source here is $info (a status-family variable, _variables.scss:15-16, with a $info-light sibling used nowhere in badge.scss), not $link-color. The correct reference is color.status.info, not color.blue, even though today they are numerically identical and swapping would look correct until one is retuned independently. See knownIssues — this is a second, more dangerous instance of the type-name-vs-token-family mismatch the survey already flagged for 'orange'.

badge/border-radius.note: badge.scss:12 — border-radius: 1em. Relative to the badge's own font-size, same reasoning as padding/inline: kept em so it follows the type, which is now absolute. Resolves to 12px. This is what produces the pill shape (radius = full font-size, i.e. >= half the text-line height).

badge/color.note: badge.scss:10 — color: variables.$white, a literal #fff (_variables.scss:29), NOT $secondary. Flat, no brandChannel. This is the text color for the base .badge and therefore for every modifier that does not override color (secondary, cool-gray, blue, green, orange — see behavior).

badge/cool-gray/background.note: badge.scss:25 — background: variables.$brand-cool-gray, which compiles to var(--uids-gray-cool) -> var(--uiowa-color-gray-500). Flat: $brand-cool-gray is a legacy core alias (like $light/$gray-light in the Background/Border foundations), not a $primary/$secondary channel, so no brandChannel flag — verified against uids-core.scss:24 (--uids-gray-cool: var(--uiowa-color-gray-500), no --brand-* involved).

badge/font-size.note: badge.scss:8. CHANGED 2026-08-20 from a raw "75%" to an absolute rem primitive, per the design system owner's ruling: "I don't want badges to flex to a larger size inside headings. So we need to make that change across all contexts." This is a DELIBERATE DESIGN CHANGE, not a fidelity correction — do not restore the percentage. 0.75rem is exactly what 75% resolved to in a 1rem context, so body/table/card-meta rendering is unchanged to the pixel; only badges in a larger ambient context (headings) stop growing. Making the base absolute is also what makes padding/inline and border-radius meaningful: they stay em, so the pill geometry still tracks the badge's own type, but that type no longer tracks the parent.

badge/font-weight.note: badge.scss:9 — font-weight: variables.$font-weight-medium, which compiles to var(--uiowa-font-weight-medium) = 500. Reused primitive, zero new minting needed.

badge/green/background.note: badge.scss:33 — background: variables.$success, a literal #00664F (_variables.scss:13). Flat. No competing primitive of the same value exists (unlike blue/orange), so no naming-collision risk here.

badge/line-height.note: badge.scss:7 — line-height: 1.67. NEW primitive proposed (see newPrimitives): no existing line-height primitive (112/125/130/140/150/160/170) equals 1.67; nearest neighbors are 160 (1.6) and 170 (1.7).

badge/orange/background.note: badge.scss:37 — background: variables.$danger, a literal #BD472A (_variables.scss:19), identical to the unused $orange variable (_variables.scss:12, itself #BD472A). Flat. type='orange' names a hue but the token family is 'danger' — already precedented in tokens/primitives/colors.json's own comment ('4.x: $danger / $orange'); the contract must state this mapping explicitly (same treatment as Button's dead 'link' value note) or it reads as a naming error. See knownIssues.

badge/padding/block.note: badge.scss:6 — padding: 0 .75em (first/vertical value of the two-value shorthand). The badge's height comes entirely from line-height x font-size; there is no vertical padding at all.

badge/padding/inline.note: badge.scss:6 — padding: 0 .75em (second/horizontal value). Relative to the badge's OWN font-size. Deliberately left as em: the em keeps this padding tied to the badge's OWN font-size, and since 2026-08-20 that font-size is an absolute 0.75rem, so it resolves to a fixed 9px in every context while still being expressed proportionally. It was a DOUBLE-relative value before that change — em on a percentage — which is what made badges grow inside headings. The em is not a placeholder for a size modifier: one was DECLINED 2026-08-21 (contracts/badge.json changes[2]) and the badge is one fixed size.

badge/primary/background.note: badge.scss:16 — background: variables.$primary, which compiles to var(--brand-primary). Same channel/ref pair as button/primary/background.

badge/primary/color.note: badge.scss:17 — color: variables.$blk, a literal #000 (_variables.scss:30), NOT variables.$secondary. Flat, no brandChannel. IMPORTANT: this differs from Button's primary/color, which IS var(--brand-secondary) (brandChannel: secondary) in button.json. The two components' 'primary' text colors have different 4.x provenance despite the identical rendered hex under the default theme — do not copy Button's brandChannel flag onto this token without re-checking the source, which is exactly the trap tokens/README's provenance rule exists to catch.

badge/secondary/background.note: badge.scss:21 — background: variables.$secondary, which compiles to var(--brand-secondary).

banner/action/button-spacing.note: banner.scss:291 — `.banner__action .bttn { margin: 0 1rem 1rem 0 }`, repeated verbatim for the `+ .bttn` case inside the container query (banner.scss:293-297). ONE token for both the inline-end and block-end slots because they are one declaration, not two decisions — the same shorthand supplies the gap between buttons in a row and the gap after a wrapped row.

banner/action/margin-top.note: banner.scss:281 — `.banner .headline + .banner__action { margin-top: 1.5rem }`. Tokenized as-shipped even though the adjacent-sibling selector CANNOT match in UIDS's own markup: Banner.vue wraps the headline in `<header class="banner__title">` while the production Twig does not, so the rule is live downstream and dead here. Recorded as a knownIssue rather than changed.

banner/bg-failsafe/on-light-overlay.note: banner.scss:463 — the light overlay's own failsafe (`--banner-bg-failsafe: white`), and banner.scss:329 for the stacked mobile treatment, where the content sits below the image on a white page rather than on top of it. FLAT: the 4.x source is the CSS keyword `white`, not a brand channel. Canonical #FFFFFF replaces the keyword in the emitted custom property; the rendered background-color (rgb(255,255,255)) is captured next to it.

banner/bg-failsafe/on-media.note: banner.scss:12 — `--banner-bg-failsafe: #{variables.$secondary}`, painted by `.banner:not([class*="bg--"])` (banner.scss:313) so a banner whose image has not loaded still reads as dark rather than transparent. Channel, not literal: 4.x $secondary.

banner/headline/margin-bottom.note: banner.scss:140 — `.banner .headline { margin-bottom: 1rem }` (space.100), the gap under both the pre-title block and the main headline. margin-top is 0 and needs no token.

banner/media/background/default.note: banner.scss:34 — `.banner .media { background: #{variables.$secondary} }`, the fill shown while the image or video is still loading. Channel: 4.x $secondary.

banner/media/background/light.note: banner.scss:473 — `.banner--overlay-light .media { background: #fff }`, the same loading fill inverted so a light-overlay banner does not flash black. FLAT: 4.x literal #fff.

banner/min-height.note: banner.scss:21 — `min-height: 15rem` (240px) on .banner, the floor that keeps a text-only banner from collapsing. No spacing primitive reaches 15rem (space.800 = 8rem is the top of the scale) and this is a component floor rather than shared vocabulary, so it stays a tier-3 literal — same treatment as brand-bar's own px heights.

banner/overlay/midpoint/default.note: banner.scss:9 — `--banner-overlay-gradient-midpoint: 40%`, where the .6 stop sits. Applies to the btt and ttb directions. Percent-valued like badge/font-size, which Figma holds as a plain FLOAT (75) — same treatment here.

banner/overlay/midpoint/ltr.note: banner.scss:456 — `.banner--overlay-ltr` re-declares the midpoint at 70%, so the left-to-right gradient holds its tint further across before falling away. The single value that makes ltr more than an angle change; pinned by the OverlayLtr fixture story.

banner/overlay/opacity/gradient/mid.note: banner.scss:10 — the second stop, painted AT the midpoint (`rgb(..., .6) var(--banner-overlay-gradient-midpoint)`); the third stop is the `transparent` keyword and has no alpha to tokenize.

banner/overlay/opacity/gradient/start.note: banner.scss:10 — the first stop of `--banner-overlay-gradient` (`rgb(var(--banner-overlay-color-rgb), .8) 0%`). Applies to all three directions; the direction only changes the angle.

banner/overlay/opacity/solid/dark.note: banner.scss:8 — `--banner-overlay-solid-opacity: .5`, the alpha of the flat scrim painted over the media by `.banner .media:after` (banner.scss:68). The COLOUR half of that rgb() lives in --banner-overlay-color-rgb, which is a bare channel triplet and is deliberately not tokenized — see contracts/banner.json geometryNotTokenized.overlay-color-channels.

banner/overlay/opacity/solid/light.note: banner.scss:461 — the `.banner--overlay-light:not([class*="bg--"])` override. A white scrim needs more alpha than a black one to carry the same legibility, which is why this is .7 rather than .5. Measured on the OverlayLight fixture story.

banner/padding/base.note: banner.scss:6 — `--banner-padding: #{variables.$gutter}` (1.25rem/20px), consumed by .banner__content's `padding: var(--banner-padding)` (banner.scss:121). $gutter IS space.125 (the primitive's own note lists it). Measured 20px at 375.

banner/padding/sm.note: banner.scss:26 — the `breakpoint(sm)` override, `--banner-padding: #{variables.$mobile-height-gutter}` (2rem/32px = space.200). THE BREAKPOINT IS IN THE NAME, not in a mobile/md/page leaf, because the switch happens at sm (768px, variables.$break-sm) and the component-tier leaves emit `@media (min-width: 980px)` — a leaf form would silently move the switch 212px and leave the 768-979 band at 20px, which the 375/980/1350 regression harness cannot see. Same reasoning tokens/README.md gives for layout.* carrying its breakpoint in the name; the consuming SCSS keeps deciding WHEN, the tokens supply WHAT.

banner/pre-title/font-size/small.note: banner.scss:232 — `.banner__pre-title.headline--small { font-size: #{variables.$h5-font-size} }`, and $h5-font-size is already `var(--uiowa-font-size-300)` (_variables.scss:68), i.e. this token re-states an existing primitive reference rather than minting a value. The large and medium pre-title sizes are fluid clamps and stay untokenized — see the contract's geometryNotTokenized.

banner/pre-title/font-weight.note: banner.scss:208 and :220 — 500, declared identically on the serif and uppercase pre-title variants. Both rules exist because each also carries its own margin; the weight itself is one decision.

banner/pre-title/line-height.note: banner.scss:204 — `.banner__pre-title { line-height: 1.1 }`. Unitless ratio. No line-height primitive matches 1.1 (the primitives are keyed by percent and start at the body/heading ratios), so it stays a tier-3 literal.

banner/pre-title/uppercase-margin-bottom.note: banner.scss:219 — `.banner__pre-title.headline.headline--uppercase { margin-bottom: 0.7rem }`, overriding the 0 the serif variant sets. No spacing primitive is 0.7rem (space.75 is 0.75rem, a different value — do NOT round to it), so this is a tier-3 literal and a 5.x consolidation candidate.

banner/text-color/on-light-fill.note: banner.scss:307 — `.banner[class*="bg--gold"], [class*="bg--white"], [class*="bg--gray"] { --banner-text-color: #{variables.$secondary} }`, and again at banner.scss:462 for the light overlay and banner.scss:328/343 for the stacked mobile treatment. $secondary IS var(--brand-secondary), so this MUST carry brandChannel or a grayscale-themed site loses the flip — the provenance rule the Buttons swap was written after. Measured #000000 on the BackgroundPattern (gold) and OverlayLight fixtures.

banner/text-color/on-media.note: banner.scss:11 — `--banner-text-color: #fff`, the base foreground over a media fill, consumed by .headline (banner.scss:138), .banner__text and its p/blockquote/heading descendants (banner.scss:240-264), and aliased into --link-color (banner.scss:13). FLAT, no brandChannel: the 4.x source is the literal #fff, not $primary/$secondary — the same provenance color/on-dark/text records for the background foundation. Emitting canonical #FFFFFF where the SCSS wrote #fff changes the custom property's text but not its rendering; the rendered .headline colour is captured alongside it in the baseline.

banner/text/margin-bottom.note: banner.scss:241 — `.banner__text { margin-bottom: 1.05rem }`. space.105 is the shipped legacy oddball step (4.x $md); reused rather than rounded, per the as-shipped rule. Measured 16.8px.

banner/video-btn/background.note: banner.scss:91 — `background: white`. FLAT: CSS keyword, not a channel.

banner/video-btn/border-color/default.note: banner.scss:89 — the colour half of `border: 1px solid white`. White-on-white against the button's own white fill: invisible by default and only doing work against the light-overlay override below. FLAT: keyword.

banner/video-btn/border-color/on-light-o.note: banner.scss:476 — `.banner--overlay-light .media .video-btn { border: 1px solid #{variables.$secondary} }`, which is what gives the control an edge once the scrim behind it is white. Channel. Not reachable from any story (the light fixture carries an image, not a video), so covered by value identity only — recorded in regression/config.json's banner comment.

banner/video-btn/border-width.note: banner.scss:89 — `border: 1px solid white`; the width half. 1px hairlines are not on any scale.

banner/video-btn/font-size.note: banner.scss:92 — `font-size: 1rem` on the button, which sizes the Font Awesome glyph in its ::after (banner.scss:99-103, re-declared 1rem there). space/font primitive font-size.100 = 1rem exactly.

banner/video-btn/size.note: banner.scss:85-86 — `.video-btn { width: 40px; height: 40px }`, the play/pause control on a video banner. A px literal in 4.x, kept px: the spacing scale is rem-based and this is a control dimension, not layout rhythm (brand-bar's tab dimensions set the same precedent).

banner/video-controls/offset/base.note: banner.scss:75-76 — `.video-controls { right: #{variables.$gutter}; bottom: #{variables.$gutter} }` (1.25rem = space.125). Measured 20px at 375.

It coincidentally equals the base h1 weight (@mixin h1 also declares $font-weight-medium-bold), but the two are independent — the token records the page-title rule, which is what has to out-specify .headline--serif. Flat: $font-weight-medium-bold is a literal 600, not a brand channel.
